title: The Bad Push
space: the student's own zone `{user}.dojo.test` and its repo; never the shared `dojo.test` zone
goal: A change was pushed to your zone an hour ago. In one commit it added a record you want to keep and a record that is sending traffic to the wrong address. Get your zone back to the right state: keep the good record, drop the bad one, and leave everything else as it was.
seed: `dojo challenge start capstone` creates `{user}/challenge-badpush` (cloned to `~/lab/challenge-badpush`) whose last commit, by someone else, adds two records at once: `{good}` (right) and `{bad}` (wrong address). Names and addresses are picked per student.
verify_text: the zone `{user}.dojo.test`: `{good}` is an A record at `198.51.100.{good_octet}`, `{bad}` is absent, the apex, `www` and `mail` are unchanged. It can't see whether history was rewritten, so the goal only asks for that.
hints: You can roll back part of a commit by editing, not only by `revert`.
isolation: the student's own repo and their own zone only.
answer: `dojo challenge start capstone`, `cd ~/lab/challenge-badpush`, `git log -p` shows the last commit added `{good}` and `{bad}`; delete the `{bad}` line by editing (or `git revert` and then re-add `{good}`), commit (no force push), `dnscontrol preview`, `dnscontrol push`, then `dojo check capstone`.
constraints: in `{user}/challenge-badpush`; your zone `{user}.dojo.test` ends up with the good record `{good}` (an A record at `198.51.100.{good_octet}`) and without the bad record `{bad}`; the apex, `www` and `mail` records are unchanged; fix it with new commits and never rewrite history (this last rule is on you, the check can't see it)
